note: Shared canonical-JSON and digest contract for the Record, the Map and the runtime. All three chains must produce identical bytes and identical digests for these inputs, or a cross-checked record is not cross-checkable. Serialisation is sorted keys, separators (",", ":"), ensure_ascii true, values normalised to JSON-native types before dumping rather than through a serialiser hook.

floats_are_refused.rule: A float is never serialised. An implementation MUST raise rather than emit a number for any float it is handed, anywhere in a payload, before hashing. Exact numbers travel as decimal strings, quantised once at the boundary.
floats_are_refused.why: Python and JavaScript both print doubles with a shortest-round-trip algorithm and still disagree: 1e-07 against 1e-7, 1e+21 against 1e21, -0.0 against 0, and 1e+16 against 10000000000000000. An outsider recomputing one of our commitments in a browser would then fail to verify an honest record.
floats_are_refused.decimal_form: Fixed-point, never scientific: format(d, 'f'), so 1E-7 is written 0.0000001 and 1E+21 is written 1000000000000000000000. An implementation must not have to reproduce another language's exponent rules.
floats_are_refused.quantisation: Six decimal places for probabilities. Quantising a non-zero value to zero is itself refused: it would seal a different claim than the one intended.

domains.note: Every digest is prefixed with a domain tag and a 0x00 separator, so two different claims about two different objects can never be confusable. An implementation that omits the tag produces digests that verify against nothing.

signatures.note: Signed bytes are the actor signature domain, a 0x00 separator, then the canonical JSON of {"actor": <envelope without its signature>, "payload": <what is being attested>}. Verification needs only the public key.

key_roles.attestation: signs what the firm writes to itself; public half stays internal
key_roles.publish: signs what the firm publishes; public half goes out with the record

pseudonyms.note: A pseudonym is sha256(domain || 0x00 || salt || 0x00 || canonical_json({field: value})) under one long-lived secret salt of at least 32 bytes. It publishes the partition without the names, so a reader can count the blocks every statistic rests on.

digest: sha256, full 64 hex characters, never truncated
